svg.title: Side-by-Side Split of the Two Analytic Engines Feeding Moments.lean in Stage 04
svg.desc: Editorial mathematical diagram of the two parallel analytic engines feeding Moments.lean in Stage 04 of the Riemann Hypothesis proof. At the top, an entry splitter takes cut Bessel amplitude sums over rational elements gamma outside R_bar_0 and routes them into two lanes. The Left Lane (cobalt, diamond markers) shows the Main Term Big-Cell Kloosterman Sieve in EnergyEstimate.lean and GlobalSieve.lean in three steps: (1) Open Reduction implies Big Cell via IsOpenElement.leadingMinor_ne_zero, where nonzero proper leading minors yield Bruhat head factorization gamma = u w_p sigma u'^{-1}; (2) Siegel's Step via prod_bandLimit_eq_gram, gramScalar_mul_headDensity, and mul_sum_norm_sum_cosetAmplitude_sq_le pairs the archimedean band-limited Gram matrix bandLimit n against the finite Kloosterman density G.lastEntryDensity / Y.massRatio while the global product formula cancels head powers p_a; (3) Entry-by-Entry One-Sided Poisson Summation via GlobalSieve.lean::sieve, prod_poissonConst_eq, and sieve_constant_le peels off n = varrho + 1 head coordinates one by one, preserving sharp constant 1 at zero frequency and absorbing nonzero frequencies into b^{-10}. Its output box gives linkSecondMoment_isOpenElement_le: at most (1 + b^{-4}) b^{-6k|S_g|} D_main nu^2. The Right Lane (emerald and amber/rust, circle and triangle markers) shows the Remaining Terms Link-Lattice Engine in RemainingTerms/Sum.lean, SiegelLemma.lean, and SchurTest.lean: (1) Near Pairs Over Agreeing Block via corank_le_and_pairDiscriminant_le and pairDiscriminant_sq_le bounds the common link Lambda_gamma intersect Lambda_gamma' with corank l <= n^3, discriminant d <= b^{n^3 f}, and congruence compression d^2 <= (2/M)^{2if} G(gamma) G(gamma'); (2) Branching on InSameLinkClass splits into Branch A (not InSameLinkClass: cross-link or g = 0, rust/amber) combining the (2/M)^{2if} congruence gain, Bombieri-Vaaler Siegel's lemma (tsum_sublatticeDiscriminant_inv_le), and weighted Schur test (amplitudeMajorant_sq_le, sum_termSize_mul_not_inSameLinkClass_le) to prove secondMoment_remainingTerms_le with tail at most b^{-kf} D_id, and Branch B (InSameLinkClass, g != 0, meeting reduction meetNorm s >= z, emerald) extracting the frame-meeting norm gain (b^{2f}/z)^k via sum_termSize_mul_inSameLinkClass_le to prove linkSecondMoment_le_of_le_meetNorm: at most (b^{2f}/z)^k D_main nu^2. At the bottom, both lanes converge into Moments.lean, establishing both the near-R_bar_0 bound (<= b^{-12} D_id implying ||P* P - 1||^2 <= b^{-12} D_X) and the whole-group second moment (<= (1 + 9 b^{-4}) D_main), accompanied by a rust callout noting the fundamental asymmetry: the Left Lane wins via genuine Fourier duality preserving exact constant 1, whereas the Right Lane uses absolute-value triangle inequality with no phase cancellation and wins via rank-k arithmetic sparsity.

g.text: ENTRY SPLITTER · CUT BESSEL AMPLITUDE SUMS OUTSIDE R0
γ ∈ Γ* = G(E) \ R0 over block (c, s, c')
◆ Open reductions s (same link, g ≠ 0) → Left Lane │ ● Cross-link, g = 0, or meeting s (meetNorm s ≥ z) → Right Lane
◆ LEFT LANE · MAIN TERM: KLOOSTERMAN SIEVE
Nonzero proper leading minors of frameProducts γ
⇒ Bruhat head factorization γ = u wp σ u'−1 (p : Fin ϱ → T0)
Removes n = ϱ + 1 head coordinates one entry at a time
Nonzero frequencies absorbed into b−10 (total ≤ 1 + b−4)
Extra b−6k gain per place in Sg where s fixes a frame vector
● RIGHT LANE · REMAINING TERMS: LINK-LATTICE ENGINE
Common link Λγ ∩ Λγ': corank l ≤ n3, discriminant d ≤ bn³f
• (2/M)2if congruence gain (or rank drop when g = 0)
Tail ≤ b−kf · Did (isolates single-link square w)
● BRANCH B · InSameLinkClass, g ≠ 0 (meetNorm s ≥ z)
• Non-open s: frame span meets s-image mod primes ∣ M
Combines open-cell sieve + cross-link/g=0 tail + meeting-reduction bounds
▲ ANALYTIC ASYMMETRY · WHY THE TWO LANES WIN DIFFERENTLY
◆ Left lane wins via genuine Fourier duality (one-sided Poisson summation on PSD kernels), preserving exact constant 1 (error ≤ b−4).
● Right lane uses absolute-value triangle inequality (no phase cancellation), winning via rank-k arithmetic sparsity ((2/M)2if, z−1 to k).
